analysis.title: Excelerate Energy Inc (EE): First Take: 3Q26 Beat; Caribbean Expansion Announced - Eliminated SoH Crossings Derisks 2027 Outlook
key_insights: EE (Buy) reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $133.5m, above the GS estimate of $128m and FactSet consensus of $129m (+5%/+4%). Stronger Terminal Services margins offset slightly softer LNG, Gas, and Power margins.

EE narrowed 2026 adj. EBITDA guidance to $495-515m from $490-515m. The GS estimate is $499m and consensus is $497m. Total capex guidance was lowered slightly to $465-485m from $465-495m, as higher growth capex was offset by lower maintenance capex.

EE plans to eliminate Strait of Hormuz crossings for both the Iraq terminal and the Colombia FSRU deployments by swapping vessels already inside or outside the Strait. In-service dates are unchanged at 2Q27 for Iraq and 1Q27 for Colombia.

GS sees the crossing elimination as proof of EE's underappreciated operational flexibility and expects it to lift investor confidence in the 2027 growth outlook. Contract rates and project returns for Iraq and Colombia are expected to drive relative performance on the next trading day.

EE announced plans to develop a Bahamas LNG Hub, a floating LNG storage and distribution terminal near Grand Bahama. Initial deliveries ramp in 1Q27 using the Jamaica platform's existing FSRU, LNG supply and logistics, and a dedicated FSU is added in 2H28 with $85-95m of guided capex.
The Bahamas project is underpinned by an 11-year agreement with AxDo Bahamas. EE expects to have additional capacity for regional customers once the FSU is deployed in 2H28.
EE signed a 5-year extension of the Sequoia contract with Petrobras, now running through 2038. EE will install a reliquefaction unit on the Sequoia during its next scheduled dry dock in 2028.

GS price targets and estimates are unchanged ahead of the earnings call. Key questions are the Bahamas hub economics and contracting, the plan to avoid Strait of Hormuz crossings, the next FSRU conversions, Iraq terminal construction steps, Jamaica optimization, Middle East operational risk and the dividend growth outlook through 2028.
GS has a 12-month $49 price target on an unlevered DCF with a 10.25% WACC and 3% terminal growth. The stock closed at $34.29 on 4 Nov 2026, implying 42.9% upside.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 adj. EBITDA beat, narrowed FY26 guidance, Caribbean expansion and the Sequoia extension support the thesis. Eliminating planned Strait of Hormuz crossings derisks the 2027 outlook.

earnings_insights: EE 3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported at $133.5m vs GS estimate $128m and FactSet consensus $129m. Prior quarter (2Q26) was $120m.

Terminals gross margin reported $116m vs GS estimate $101m (+14.2%). LNG, Gas and Power gross margin reported $40m vs GS estimate $44m (-8.3%). Adjusted gross margin reported $156m vs GS estimate $145m (+7.4%).
Terminal Services revenue reported $166m vs GS estimate $156m. LNG, Gas and Power revenue reported $132m vs GS estimate $312m, with cost of LNG, gas and power sales $91m vs GS estimate $268m.
Dividend reported at $0.09 per share, in line with the GS estimate and up 12.5% from $0.08 in 3Q25.
FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance narrowed to $495-515m (company guidance) from $490-515m prior. The GS estimate is $499m and consensus is $497m. FY26 capex guidance is $465-485m, down from $465-495m.
GS forecasts (estimates, not reported): FY26E EBITDA $498.8m, FY26E EPS $1.41, 9/26E quarterly EPS $0.34, FY27E EBITDA $575.2m and FY27E EPS $1.67.
risk_factors: Higher global gas pricing could weigh on global LNG demand.
A longer-than-expected geopolitical conflict in the Middle East.
Higher-than-expected conversion costs for incremental FSRUs and market competition for FSRU deployments.
Higher-than-expected LNG supply costs for the Iraq project.
Counterparty credit risk and customer FX convertibility risk.
Balance sheet over-extension and/or equity funding needs.
geopolitical: Conflict in the Middle East and Strait of Hormuz transit risk. EE plans to avoid Strait crossings for its Iraq terminal and Colombia FSRU deployments by using FSRUs already in or outside the region and sourcing LNG within the region.
